description: Dispatch an async job that reads the Marketo activity log -- what leads actually DID or had done to them (emails sent/delivered, alerts, sales emails, campaign requests, data value changes) -- and return {job_id, status} in milliseconds; the read itself runs in a background worker. Poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished result: path, columns, row_count, and truncated. Pass since_datetime (ISO-8601, second-granularity -- a fractional-seconds component is floor-truncated before the paging-token request because Marketo otherwise rewinds that window to midnight UTC). activity_type_ids is mandatory (1-10 ids from list_activity_types); lead_ids is an optional server-side filter (max 30). Pages internally across Marketo's own 300-per-call vendor ceiling up to the effective row limit -- no next_page_token or continuation parameter exists on this verb. Defaults to 500. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 5,000) -- both required together, refused rather than clamped above 5,000, and refused at DISPATCH time (before any job is created). Beyond the hard cap: no resumption, re-invoke with a later since_datetime. PAGING (on the finished job): moreResult is the ONLY usable vendor continuation signal internally -- Adobe documents this endpoint always returns a token, so token presence can't terminate the loop (unlike get_leads/list_campaigns/list_static_lists), and a short or empty page does NOT mean the end of the data. Its reliability is documented but UNMEASURED on live traffic; the one live measurement of moreResult anywhere found it violated on list_campaigns, so truncated=false on the finished job is only as honest as Marketo's own flag -- there is no fallback if it under-reports. Prefer requesting stable ID and status fields for validation over email or other PII-bearing fields.
embedding_description: Check what actually HAPPENED to a Marketo person after a write -- email sent/delivered, alert fired, campaign ran, data value changed -- an after-the-fact audit, not a person lookup. Async: a background job builds a workspace TSV of activity events while dispatch returns a job_id in milliseconds; retrieve the finished export with check_marketo_job_status.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Marketo activity log export job dispatched
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dict with job_id (pass to check_marketo_job_status to retrieve the finished export) and status (always 'queued' -- this verb never waits for the vendor read).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the job was dispatched and give the job_id; tell the caller to poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) for the finished TSV handle (path, row_count, columns, truncated) and to lead with whether any NOTIFYING activity appeared once it lands -- that is almost always why the caller asked. Do not claim any activity happened OR did not happen from THIS verb's response -- it never carries activity data.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Never report 'no notifications were sent' from THIS verb's response, and never do so from check_marketo_job_status's result either unless its truncated is false -- a truncated read is not evidence of silence, only an unmeasured vendor flag's best account of one.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validate the activity-log request and dispatch a background job to read it and write it to a tab-separated file in the operator's workspace, up to an acknowledged override ceiling, to verify what a write actually caused. This verb only validates and dispatches -- it never talks to Marketo directly, not even to mint the paging token.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: These are DISPATCH-time errors only -- caught before any vendor call is made (including the paging-token mint), so no job was created. marketo.invalid_params: activity_type_ids was omitted/empty/exceeded 10, since_datetime was missing or not ISO-8601-shaped, lead_ids exceeded 30, output_tsv_path was missing, its parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, row_limit exceeded the 5,000 hard cap, or session_id/flow_id were missing from the calling context. marketo.export_path_refused: the path is not absolute, not a .tsv, or not contained under any operator-configured export_allowed_roots entry (an empty export_allowed_roots refuses every export by default). Vendor-side faults (marketo.auth_failed, marketo.permission_denied, marketo.partition_access_denied, marketo.rate_limited, or an invalid since_datetime Marketo itself rejects at token-mint time) can NOT surface here -- they only appear later, in check_marketo_job_status's error field, once the background worker actually calls Marketo.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: marketo.invalid_params: call list_activity_types, supply 1-10 returned ids, and supply since_datetime as an ISO-8601 instant -- it is required on every call, there is no continuation-token alternative. Split lead_ids into batches of 30. For the override pair, pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-item default); a row_limit above 5,000 is refused outright, not clamped. marketo.export_path_refused: pass an ABSOLUTE path ending in .tsv under a configured workspace root. Once dispatch succeeds, poll check_marketo_job_status(job_id) -- if THAT reports an error, its guidance covers the vendor-side classes (auth, permission, partition, rate limit, or a since_datetime the vendor itself rejects).
